text:
anya: Quick question — planning key rotation for customer envelopes next quarter. We need an RBAC + audit plan that lets us do manual rewrap jobs safely and keep backward compatibility for old ciphertext headers. Thoughts?
chris: +1. Two big concerns: who can trigger rewraps (least privilege) and how we capture rewrap events in audit logs (so we can prove data lineage).
luis: For AWS: prefer reEncrypt instead of decrypting plaintext in-app. Use a dedicated rewrap service role with kms:ReEncrypt and kms:DescribeKey only. No plaintext ever reaches app code.
oliver: On GCP you can do a similar approach with CMEK and the Asymmetric vs Symmetric difference matters. Rewraps are server-side if you use Cloud KMS decrypt/encrypt, but make sure the service account has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter and audit logging enabled.
anya: Good notes. What about Azure Key Vault? Any special RBAC quirks?
chris: Azure: use Key Vault access policies or RBAC depending on tenant. The rewrap service should use wrapKey/unwrapKey permissions only. Avoid full key delete permissions. Also enable Purge Protection + Soft Delete for safety.
luis: Audit log details: ensure we capture the key id, requestor identity, source IP, and operation type (ReEncrypt/Encrypt/Decrypt). For AWS CloudTrail, filter on kms:ReEncrypt and look for requestParameters.ciphertextBlob. For GCP, check Cloud Audit Logs with protoPayload.methodName like "google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Encrypt".
ops-sre: We should add an explicit header version field to ciphertext metadata so the runtime knows which KEK schema was used. That lets old clients still decrypt older headers while new writes use v2.
anya: Proposal: staged rollout plan: (1) create new KEK; (2) deploy rewrap worker in staging with small canary; (3) run dry-run mode where worker logs intended rewrap but doesn't write; (4) run batched rewrap copying to new ciphertext with versioned header; (5) switch read preference to accept v2; (6) retire old KEK after verifying logs.
chris: +emoji :thumbsup: Add RBAC step between 2 and 3: create a temporary "km-rewrap" role scoped to the env and require two approvers (security + infra) to grant it. Revoke after completion.
oliver: For the dry-run, output a hash diff but do NOT log plaintext. Sample AWS CLI rewrap we used in staging: ```aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://old.ct --destination-key-id alias/new-kek --output text > new.ct``` (we keep blobs binary and audit the operation only).
luis: Monitoring: track decrypt_errors/sec, rewrap_failures, time-to-complete per object, and CloudTrail/CAL gaps. Raise alert if decrypt_errors spike or if rewrap throughput lags SLA.
ops-sre: Backout plan: pause rewrap workers, revoke rewrap role, and set traffic to serve only v1 ciphertexts. We need to ensure reads for v1 remain supported until manual fallback is done.
anya: How do we guarantee no plaintext leakage during rewrap?
chris: Key point: use KMS re-encrypt primitives (server-side). If you must decrypt and re-encrypt client-side, do it in a locked ephemeral worker with no persistent logs, and use memory sanitization and ephemeral compute. But avoid if possible.
luis: Also consider using Grants (AWS KMS grants) for short-lived permissions rather than broad IAM roles. Grants can be constrained to particular key usage and caller, easier to audit.
oliver: Compatibility: include a header like: {"v":2,"k":"alias/new-kek","alg":"AEAD"} in envelope metadata. Older readers check v and use old KEK lookup. New readers accept both.
security-bot: Alert configured: kms.rewrap.job.failure > 5 in 10m => page #eng-oncall. Audit log retention: 1y for CloudTrail, 6mo for GCP by default — request extended retention for audits.
anya: One more: vulnerability triage — if a KEK is suspected compromised mid-roll, what's emergency flow?
chris: Emergency: (1) suspend rewraps, (2) immediately create replacement KEK with different key material, (3) run prioritized rewrap for high-risk objects (PII) first, (4) rotate any derived keys, (5) produce audit pack with pre/post rewrap identifiers and request legal/infosec review.
oliver: Document the SLAs for rewraps and expected performance impact on batch jobs. Some ETL windows will need longer maintenance windows.
anya: Thanks — I'll draft the runbook and RBAC matrix. I'll call out AWS/GCP/Azure differences and include the CLI snippets and header spec. Anyone want to pair on review tomorrow?
chris: I can pair at 10am PT.
luis: I'll review the audit log queries and retention notes.
security-bot: Runbook created: https://confluence.internal/redwood/security/kms-rewrap-runbook (stub) :eyes:
ops-sre: Adding a canary job to cron for tomorrow 02:00 UTC, will ping when ready.
